prose.article: Ashima appears only once in the Old Testament, in 2 Kings 17:30, where the men of Hamath are said to have made an idol called Ashima. The name is treated as a proper noun — a specific god brought into Samaria by foreign settlers after the Assyrian deportation. Because it is a foreign deity name of non-Hebrew origin, it carries no broader Hebrew semantic range; it simply identifies this particular idol among a list of pagan gods.
prose.caution: Ashima is a hapax legomenon (appearing only once in the OT), its precise identity and background are debated among scholars, and its exact linguistic origin remains uncertain.

prose.def: A foundation or base, used once in Isaiah to describe something ruined or collapsed.
prose.article: This rare word appears only once in the entire Old Testament, in Isaiah 16:7, where it refers to a foundation — specifically in the context of ruin and destruction. The Strong's definition connects it to the idea of pressing down firmly, suggesting a base or supporting structure. Because it occurs only this single time, the KJV renders it simply as "foundation," and there is no broader usage pattern to draw on for context.
